title: Customizing Accrual Calculation
author: I748612
text:
Purchase Order Accruals: Define Accrual Methods 
 Accrual Item Type 
 The accrual item type determines which amounts are subject to accrual and whether full or delta postings should be applied. 
 Accrual Calculation Logic 
 The accrual item type does not define the algorithm for calculating accrual amounts per period. Instead, this logic is specified in a separate Customizing entity called the accrual method . 
 Accrual Method as an ABAP Class Method 
 An accrual method functions similarly to an ABAP class method. Each accrual method is linked to a specific ABAP class method or function module, where the accrual calculation algorithm is implemented. 
 Default Accrual Methods 
 SAP provides the most commonly used accrual algorithms as standard Customizing content. 
 Custom Accrual Methods 
 Customers can develop their own accrual methods by creating an ABAP class that implements the interface IF_ACE_CFG_METHOD . 

 Purchase Order Accruals: SAP-Delivered Accrual Methods 
 SAP provides several default accrual methods as part of its standard customizing content. These methods serve different purposes: 
 Accrual Methods for Planned Costs Some accrual methods are designed to calculate and distribute planned costs for a purchase order item over its lifecycle. The chosen method determines how these costs are allocated across fiscal periods, directly impacting the accrual amounts posted in each period. 
 Technical Accrual Methods Other methods, such as ZERO_AMNT , DERIVED , and PLN-ACT , are used for technical purposes. For example: 
 If an accrual item becomes obsolete (e.g., due to the deletion of a purchase order item), the Accrual Engine automatically assigns the ZERO_AMNT method. This ensures that in the next accrual posting run, the accrual amount is reset to zero. 

 Accrual Engine: Calculation of Periodic Accrual Amounts 
 Key Principles 
 Under IFRS , accruals may be posted when there is a potential debt to an external legal entity (e.g., a supplier). 
 The logic for determining this debt and the related accrual amount is use-case specific . 
 The Accrual Engine supports all potential algorithms, allowing for: 
 Custom accrual methods via ABAP class methods (configurable in Customizing). 
 Customer-defined algorithms in addition to SAP’s default settings. 
 Standard Accrual Calculation Process 
 The Accrual Engine follows a three-step approach to calculate accruals: 
 Determine Planned and Actual Costs 
 Planned Costs : The amount of goods/services received up to a key date. 
 Example: For a purchase order item, the system uses the delivery schedule to estimate received quantities. 
 These amounts are stored as Planned Costs in the Accrual Engine. 
 Actual Costs : The amount already posted (e.g., supplier invoices for non-valuated goods receipts). 
 The system selects all invoices with a posting date before the key date . 
 These amounts are stored as Actual Costs in the Accrual Engine. 
 Calculate the Accrual Amount 
 The system computes the difference: Accrual Amount = Planned Costs – Actual Costs 
 If the result is greater than zero , it represents the debt to the supplier. 
 The accrual amount is stored as Accruals (ACCRL) in the Accrual Engine. 
 Purchase Order Accruals: Calculation of Periodic Accrual Amounts 
 The Purchase Orders Accruals application is built on the Accrual Engine , which provides flexibility in accrual calculations while offering specialized features for a three-step accrual approach . 
 Key Features of the Accrual Engine 
 Supports a wide range of accrual calculation algorithms. 
 Includes tailored functionalities for the three-step accrual method , which involves: 
 First Step: The Accrual Engine computes: 
 Planned Costs (expected expenses) 
 Actual Costs (recorded expenses) 
 Second Step: The accrual amount is determined by subtracting Actual Costs from Planned Costs . 
 If the result is negative, it is set to zero (since accruals cannot be negative from a business perspective). 
 Optional: Additional accrual item types may be included (e.g., parked invoices for further analysis). 
 Exclusive Features for the Three-Step Approach 
 Period-End Closing Transaction for Review/Approval: 
 Allows reviewers/approvers to adjust accrual amounts. 
 Displays three key columns: 
 Planned Costs 
 Actual Costs 
 Accrual Amount 
 Note: The Planned Costs and Actual Costs columns are only populated when using the three-step method. 
 User-Friendly Accrual Object Display (e.g., Transaction POACTREE03): 
 Automatically presents Planned Costs, Actual Costs, and Accrual Amounts in a consolidated table for easy comparison. 
 Purchase Order Accruals: Accrual Methods for Planned Costs (PLN_DSNVGR) 
 Purchase Order Accruals: Accrual Methods for Planned Costs (Linearization) 
 Accrual Method: PLN-ACT (Planned Costs Reduced by Actual Costs)

title: 三个小插件，让 OpenCode Desktop 使用更顺手
author: LPhilip
text:
背景 
 最近迁移到 OpenCode 后，用它做日常工作，遇到了一些不顺手的地方，比方说：主题风格不习惯、文档阅读别扭，以及执行过程中的反馈显示不好理解。 
 AI时代，想出手时就可以出手，直接折腾AI做了一些改动尝试。 
 这个项目分享这些改动和背后的思路，不是官方的迁移报告。 
 这是个人项目，不是 SAP 官方产品。 
 逻辑上来讲这些代码都是跨平台的，但插件整体只在我当前的 Windows 电脑和当前使用的 OpenCode Desktop 上测试过。其他电脑、版本和操作系统（包括 macOS）均未验证。 
 解决什么问题 
 截图说明： 所有截图均使用虚构的演示数据，不对应真实客户案例或事故。 
 Fiori Horizon：换成接近 SAP Fiori 的风格 
 个人觉得OpenCode自带的主题太单调，想换成更接近 SAP Fiori 的浅色风格。它既调整主对话区的展示颜色，也调整文档浏览区 Markdown 的显示样式，包括标题、表格、引用和行内代码。不只是换一个背景色，也不是 SAP 官方主题。 

 Workspace Navigation：找文件更全，打开后知道它在哪 
 文件面板自带的搜索不够全，打开文件后也不会主动展开父目录、选中对应节点。搜索增强沿用原来的输入框，按文件名和路径查找，并把隐藏和 gitignored 目录中的文件纳入搜索；输入多个词可以缩小范围，例如 report md 、 docs report md 。 
 打开文件后自动展开父目录、选中并定位文件的功能，目前由 UX Enhancements 实现。想同时获得搜索和文件树跟随，需要启用这两个插件。 

 UX Enhancements：过程反馈更清楚，结果更方便查看 
 刚开始用 OpenCode 时，总觉得它有点慢。但不确定是真的执行慢，还是界面变化不明显，让等待显得更久。所以我先想执行反馈做得更清楚：现在在做什么、执行到哪一步、什么时候结束。这改善的是等待时的体验，不代表模型或工具执行得更快。 
 工具执行时自动展开，并显示命令和操作摘要；后续回答出现或执行结束后自动收拢。需要细节时可以重新展开，原始命令和输出仍保留。 
 回复中已有的文件路径（包括末尾文件清单里的路径）可以直接点击，在右侧边栏打开。插件不会替模型生成文件清单。 
 文档可以铺满右侧面板，同时暂时隐藏对话，方便专心阅读；再次切换即可回到对话。这是应用内全宽阅读，不是 Windows 全屏。 
 此外，打开文件时会在文件树中展开父目录、选中并定位文件；也可以编辑本地文本文件，或复制文件内容和路径。 
 三个插件可以一起使用，也可以只复制需要的插件文件夹。搜索和 UX 不依赖主题；这些插件不会额外调用模型，也不修改 OpenCode 的安装文件。 
 插件怎么工作 
 OpenCode 读取每个插件的 package.json ，找到并加载入口。GUI 代码分两部分运行：窗口里的 setup 负责界面，Electron 主进程里的 main 负责本地文件操作，两者通过 IPC 通信。 

 主题只改变显示样式。Navigation 合并原搜索和本地路径索引，不读文件正文；远程工作区不做本地补搜。UX 根据会话状态更新过程展示，检查已有文件引用后再添加链接；全宽阅读复用原审查按钮，保存则通过 IPC 检查并写入本地文件。 
 这些都是运行代码的 Plugin，不是给 agent 提供任务步骤的 Skill，也不是接入外部工具的 MCP；三个插件不依赖 Skill 或 MCP。 
 源码在 plugins/ 。 .cjs 文件是手写源码，也可以直接作为 GUI 入口加载。主题使用 OpenCode 的 Theme 和 Style 接口；搜索包装和部分 UX 行为依赖当前桌面界面结构，OpenCode 更新后可能需要调整。 
 按自己的习惯改 
 这里主要分享的是个思路，不是我的配色。 
 套用星爷的话： 其实创作这个东西是很主观滴，不过你们滴批评我是一定会跟进滴 。 
 审美这个东西也是很主观的，你个人的口味也是可以让 AI 跟进的。让AI帮你改，一次改一点，改到你满意为止。 
 各插件旁边的 test.cjs 是可选开发测试，不是安装步骤，OpenCode 日常使用不会运行它们。不需要另外维护编译流程或发布包。 
 安装 
 在 : GitHub repo - opencode-desktop-plugins 选择 Code → Download ZIP ，解压后，把 plugins 里需要的插件文件夹复制到： 
 ~/.config/opencode/plugins 
 ~ 表示用户主目录，实际路径例如： 
 Windows ： C:\Users\<your user>\.config\opencode\plugins 
 macOS ： /Users/<your user>/.config/opencode/plugins 
 把 <your user> 换成自己的用户目录名。Windows 文件资源管理器请用实际路径，不要直接输入 ~ ；macOS 可在 Finder 的“前往文件夹”中输入 ~/.config/opencode/plugins 。macOS 路径只是安装位置参考，插件尚未在 Mac 上验证。 
 安装、使用和移除步骤见 Windows 手工指南 。

title: POAC: Customizing details
author: I748612
text:
Ledger and Ledger Group in Accrual Engine 
 Assigning Ledger Groups to Accrual Item Types In the IMG activity Define Accrual Item Types, you specify the ledger groups where accrual postings should be made by assigning ledger groups to accrual item types. 
 Handling Different Fiscal Year Variants If you need to calculate and post accruals for certain ledgers using different fiscal year variants, you may define multiple ledger groups: 
 One ledger group where the representative ledger uses fiscal year variant X. 
 Another ledger group where the representative ledger uses fiscal year variant Y. 
 Non-Overlapping Ledger Groups Ensure that the ledger groups do not overlap; otherwise, accruals may be posted twice. 
 Consistent Ledger Group Assignment The same ledger groups must be assigned to all accrual item types: 
 ACCRL (Accrual) 
 ACTCST (Actual Cost) 
 PLNCST (Planned Cost) 

 Accrual Item Types Settings for Planned Costs, Actual Costs, and Accruals 
 In the IMG activity Define Accrual Item Types (under Item Type Settings for Ldrgrp incl. Repr. Ledger ), an entry must be configured for each of the following three item types: 
 PLNCST – Planned Costs 
 ACTCST – Actual Costs (posted invoices/goods receipts) 
 ACCRL – Accruals (calculated as Planned Costs minus Actual Costs ) 
 Key Requirements: These three accrual item types must have identical settings for: 
 Ledger Group 
 Frequency 
 Handling of Currency 

 Display of Ledger and Ledger Group in the Accrual Engine 
 Accrual Calculation Scope 
 The Accrual Engine performs accrual calculations at the ledger level , determining accrual amounts for individual ledgers rather than ledger groups. 
 Current Limitation 
 Presently, the Accrual Engine only calculates accrual amounts for the representative ledger of a ledger group. 
 Posting of Accruals 
 The ledger group assigned to an accrual item type is used for posting accruals. 
 The accrual amount calculated for the representative ledger is posted to all ledgers within that ledger group. 
 Display in Accrual Engine Screens 
 In Accrual Engine screens—such as the accrual objects display (transaction POACTREE03 ) or review and approval screens (transactions FACRARVW *)—only the ledger group is displayed by default. 

 Ledger and Currency Types in Accrual Engine 
 In the IMG activity Define Accrual Item Types , you specify the ledger groups for accrual postings. The system automatically performs the following assignments: 
 Assigns the representative ledger of the ledger group to the accrual item type. 
 Assigns currency type 00 (transaction currency) to the Accrual Engine. 
 Currency Handling for Type 00 
 For purchase order accruals , you must define the currency handling as A – By Accrual Engine . This setting ensures that: 
 The Accrual Engine calculates accrual amounts in this currency type. 
 Since the accrual object is created by transferring the purchase order into the Accrual Engine, the only available currency is the purchase order currency , which is treated as the transaction currency.

title: Accrual Engine Data Structure - Purchase Order Accruals
author: Ujhelyi_Zsuzsi
text:
Hierarchical Structure of Accrual Objects: 
 Accrual Objects : These represent the overall business transaction, similar to a contract header. 
 Accrual Subobjects : These can be regarded as contract items. For each contract item, you might need to post accruals for various amounts, such as expected costs, interests, and bonuses for sales representatives. 
 Accrual Item Types : Each amount to be accrued within an accrual subobject is represented by an accrual item type. 
 Accrual Items : Accrual item types and ledgers define an accrual item. Each accrual subobject has at least one accrual item assigned to it. 
 Accrual Methods : For each accrual item, an algorithm (called the accrual method) is assigned to calculate the accrual amounts for different periods. 
 Data Structure in the Accrual Engine for Purchase Orders: 
 Accrual Objects : In the application Purchase Order Accruals, an accrual object represents a purchase order. 
 Accrual Subobjects : An accrual subobject represents a purchase order item, which is further subdivided based on the account assignments given in the purchase order. 

 Information Stored for Each Accrual Item 
 For each combination of accrual item type and ledger, the following information is stored for the accrual item: 
 Total Amount to be Accrued : The overall amount that requires accrual. 
 Accrual Method : The calculation algorithm used to determine the periodic accrual amounts. 
 Key Principle of the Accrual Engine 
 A fundamental principle of the Accrual Engine is that for each amount to be calculated, a separate accrual item type must be created in Customizing. 
 Purpose in Purchase Order Accruals 
 The objective of the Accrual Engine in purchase order accruals is to calculate an amount that will be posted as accruals at the end of each fiscal period. To achieve this, at least one accrual item type must be created in Customizing. SAP provides the accrual item type ACCRL for this purpose. 
 Recommended Approach: Three-Step Process 
 While theoretically one accrual item type could suffice, using multiple accrual item types enhances transparency. The recommended process involves defining three accrual item types: 
 Planned Costs (PLNCST) : Calculates the planned costs of the purchase order item for each period. 
 Actual Costs (ACTCST) : Calculates the actual costs of the purchase order item for each period, based on either goods receipt postings or supplier invoice postings. 
 Accruals (ACCRL) : Calculates the difference between planned and actual costs, ensuring the resulting amount remains positive. If actual costs exceed planned costs, the difference is set to zero. 
 Configuring Accrual Item Types 
 If you follow the recommended three-step approach, define the following accrual item types to ensure the Accrual Engine calculates accruals using the correct algorithms: 
 Planned Costs (PLNCST) : 
 Calculates the planned costs based on the delivery schedule or an even distribution of the PO item’s net amount over a specific period (linear approach). 
 Actual Costs (ACTCST) : 
 Calculates actual costs from either: 
 Goods receipt postings (if valuated goods receipts are used). 
 Supplier invoice postings (if no or non-valuated goods receipts). 
 Accruals (ACCRL) : 
 Configured to calculate the difference between planned and actual costs, ensuring the result is always a positive amount. If the actual amount exceeds the planned amount, the difference is set to zero. 
 Flexibility in Approach 
 While the Customizing process for Purchase Order Accruals is designed for the three-step approach, it is possible to work with only one accrual item type (ACCRL). However, the three-step approach is recommended for transparency and comprehensive tracking of accrual calculations. 
 By defining these accrual item types, you can ensure that the Accrual Engine calculates the accrual amounts for each period accurately and transparently. 

 Screenshot from Transaction “Display Purchase Order” (ME23N) 
 SAP provides the following three predefined accrual item types: 
 PLNCST : For planned costs. 
 ACTCST : For actual costs. 
 ACCRL : For accruals. 
 Defining Relationships Between Accrual Item Types 
 In the "Define Accrual Item Types" activity, you establish the relationship between these three accrual item types. This informs the Accrual Engine that the periodic amounts for ACCRL are calculated by subtracting ACTCST from PLNCST, keeping only positive amounts. 
 Activating Review and Approval Processes 
 If you wish to activate a review and/or approval process for periodic accruals, you need to use an additional accrual item type. This accrual item type will contain the reviewed/approved periodic accrual amounts. 
 Predefined Accrual Item Types 
 SAP delivers the following predefined accrual item types: 
 PLNCST : For planned costs. 
 ACTCST : For actual costs. 
 ACCRL : For accruals. 

 In order to use the three-step approach for calculating accruals, you must define the relationship between the three accrual item types for planned costs (PLNCST), actual costs (ACTCST), and the resulting accruals (ACCRL). 
 You can do this using Customizing activity Define Accrual Item Types 

 Accrual Engine Calculation and Application Component 
 After assigning the item types  PLNCST  (planned costs) and  ACTCST  (actual costs) to  ACCRL  (accruals) in customizing, the Accrual Engine will automatically calculate the accruals as planned costs minus actual costs. At runtime, during the calculation of periodic accrual amounts, the Accrual Engine will determine the amount for  ACCRL  by subtracting the amount for  ACTCST  from the amount for  PLNCST . 
 Application Component in the Accrual Engine 
 The Accrual Engine includes the field  "COMP"  (application component) as a key field in all its database tables. Each application based on the Accrual Engine is defined as an application component, and each component has its own unique value in the field  "COMP" . 
 Field Value for Purchase Order Accruals : The  "COMP"  field value for Purchase Order Accruals is  POAC . 
 Customizing Settings : All customizing settings related to the Accrual Engine include the  "COMP"  field as a key field. This field is visible as a read-only field in the corresponding customizing views. 
 Naming Convention 
 All ABAP repository objects, such as transactions and programs, belonging to the application component  POAC , follow a specific naming convention: 
 Prefix : These objects have the prefix  POAC_ . 

 Configuring Accrual Item Types 
 For each accrual item type, you can specify: 
 Whether its amounts will be posted by the Accrual Engine. 
 Whether its amounts are used for calculation or display purposes only. 
 Posting Amounts for Accrual Item Types 
 If the amounts are to be posted, the accrual item type must be assigned to one or more posting schemas in the IMG activity:  Accruals Management -> Accrual Postings -> Assign Accrual Item Types to Journal Entry Types and Posting Schemas . 
 Default Settings for Pre-Delivered SAP Content 
 In the pre-delivered SAP content, accruals are calculated as planned costs minus actual costs. The following default settings apply: 
 ACCRL : Only the amounts of accrual item type ACCRL will be posted. ACCRL is assigned to some posting schemas. 
 PLNCST and ACTCST : These accrual item types will not be posted. Their amounts are calculated as intermediate steps to determine the final accruals (ACCRL). As a result, they are not assigned to a posting schema. 
 Required Postings for ACCRL 
 At least periodic postings are required for ACCRL: 
 The transaction type  PP  (Periodic Posting) is assigned to the corresponding posting schema  SAP_ACE_PP . 
 Optional Posting Assignments for ACCRL 
 You can optionally assign the following transaction types to posting schemas for accrual item type ACCRL: 
 UP  (Utilization Posting) and  FP  (Release Posting)

title: Merge Cells SAP Analytics Cloud Tables 2026 Q4 QRC
author: GregBotticchio
text:
When an outer dimension repeats the same value across multiple consecutive rows or columns, the table header becomes cluttered with identical labels, obscuring the grouping structure the layout is meant to communicate. Restructuring the data model or adding calculated objects were the only workarounds, both adding unnecessary complexity. 
 With the 2026 Q4 QRC , SAP Analytics Cloud introduces cell merging for repeated dimension member names, a display-level mechanism that visually unifies consecutive identical header cells into a single spanned cell, producing publication-quality layouts without touching the underlying data model. 

 Opt-In Cell Merging Per Dimension 
 Cell merging is opt-in per dimension, available on any flat dimension, structure, or calculation in the table widget, on both the Rows axis (vertical spans) and the Columns axis (horizontal spans). It is purely visual: the underlying data grid, calculations, sorting, filtering, and write-back are entirely unaffected. No data model changes are required. 
 ⚠️ Cell merging is only available in flat, non-hierarchical presentation mode. Switching a dimension to hierarchical display will disable merging for that dimension. (Support of hierarchical dimensions and "show only leaves" is an enhancement planned for the near future). 

 [SCREENSHOT: Table widget with cell merging enabled on an outer dimension in the Rows axis, showing consecutive identical year labels merged into a single spanned cell] 

 Configurable Label Position 
 Designers can choose where the member label appears within a merged span: First Cell, Last Cell, or Middle. The choice is free and independent per dimension, centered labels suit compact tables, whilst first-cell labels align with the reading direction of most business reports. 

 Dynamic Recomputation 
 Merged spans recompute automatically whenever the table layout changes. After a sort, filter, scroll, hierarchy change, or data refresh. The visual grouping always reflects the current state of the table, with no manual reconfiguration required. 

 Export-Ready: Excel and PDF 
 Excel exports use native cell merging, preserving the exact visual structure as proper merged ranges in the spreadsheet. PDF exports render the table exactly as it appears on screen. What designers build is what stakeholders receive, across every output format. 

 Additional Capabilities 
 Cell merging also integrates with: 
 Ad-hoc cell styling : merging does not override or reset cell-level formatting. 
 "Keep Member Names Visible" : both features can be used together where the layout benefits. 
 Scripting API: developers can activate or deactivate merging per dimension programmatically. 

 Why This Matters 
 Repeated header labels impose a real cognitive cost on every reader who has to parse grouping structure manually. Cell merging removes that cost with a single toggle, no model changes, no workarounds, no compromise on data integrity. For designers producing reports for executive audiences, customer-facing dashboards, or print distribution, this brings SAP Analytics Cloud tables to the standard of publication-quality layouts that stakeholders expect.

title: Supply Chain AI Must Do More Than Inform; It Must Help Businesses Act
author: Devesh Mishra
text:
I’ve spent more than 25 years building and scaling supply chain operations before joining SAP to lead SAP Supply Chain Management. The decision came down to something I kept encountering throughout my career: the companies with the deepest understanding of their own operations are the ones best positioned to put AI to work. 
 Orchestrate your supply chain to stay ahead and exceed expectations 

 Learn how 

 And nobody sits closer to those operations than SAP. In every customer conversation I have, I hear a similar tension: leaders know that AI will reshape their supply chains. But they need software that understands their business processes well enough to move from experimentation to impact. That challenge, and SAP’s foundation to meet it, is what brought me here. 

 What excites me most about this moment is what I call “the art of the possible,” looking beyond how things work today and imagining what best-in-class could look like if we took advantage of capabilities that simply were not available before. But expanding the art of the possible does not, by itself, create meaningful innovation. 

 For decades, companies have invested heavily in planning, manufacturing, procurement, and logistics systems that provide valuable visibility. But when a supplier misses a shipment, demand unexpectedly increases, or transportation capacity disappears, people remain essential to connect the dots across systems and functions. By the time they do, the business may already be reacting to the problem rather than getting ahead of it. 

 What becomes possible when the supply chain is a modern decision engine 

 Imagine an illustrative scenario: a supplier delay threatens production and several important customer orders. Traditionally, a planning system might generate an alert, leaving teams to determine the implications and coordinate a response. An intelligent system could go further by identifying which customer commitments are at risk, assessing available inventory across locations, evaluating whether production schedules should change, and comparing alternative transportation routes or suppliers. 

 Each option involves tradeoffs. Expediting a shipment might protect a high-priority customer order but increase costs. Reallocating inventory could preserve one commitment while creating shortages elsewhere. Adjusting production might minimize disruption but affect other delivery schedules. 

 Humans evaluate these interconnected decisions against the outcomes that matter for the business, rather than optimizing each function independently. 

 Success is measured by whether the response reduced missed customer commitments, protected revenue, limited incremental logistics costs, and avoided unnecessary inventory. Comparing results against the original plan helps the system improve future recommendations. 

 That is a fundamentally different model. Competitive advantage increasingly depends on how quickly an organization can turn change into coordinated action. 

 Autonomy should remove waiting, not people 

 As AI assumes a greater role in these decisions, we also need to be precise about what we mean by autonomy. The art of the possible lies in the absence of unnecessary waiting—not removing humans from the loop. Constructing a false competition between humans and machines creates a direct obstacle to delivering autonomy. Instead, we should be laser-focused on eliminating unnecessary work and latency while allowing people to focus their judgment where it creates the most value. 

 That also means we need to have a more sophisticated conversation about AI accuracy. An agent making a low-risk, reversible decision does not require the same confidence threshold as one making a decision with significant financial, customer, safety, or compliance implications. The question is not simply whether an AI system is “accurate.” It is whether it is sufficiently reliable for the particular decision it is being trusted to make. 

 Enterprise AI must earn the right to act 

 Before AI can be trusted to make operational decisions, it must progressively earn trust. A system might initially recommend responses while planners review its reasoning, compare alternatives, and decide whether to act. Organizations can then measure how those recommendations perform against actual outcomes, including whether they protect customer commitments, respect business constraints, and deliver expected improvements. 

 As reliability becomes more tangible, businesses can then feel more empowered to authorize AI to execute defined, lower-risk actions within established limits. More consequential actions should continue to require human approval, with transparent reasoning, documented decisions, and the ability to intervene. 

 This is how AI earns the right to act, and this is where SAP has an important role to play. Our applications connect critical business processes across planning and execution, providing the operational context needed to understand how one decision affects another. By combining that context with enterprise policies, permissions and auditable processes, we can help organizations move toward coordinated AI-driven action without sacrificing control. 

 We are already seeing the foundations of this approach emerge. For example, SAP’s Supply Chain Planning Assistant can help planners identify potential root causes of planning issues and recommend corrective actions. Takeda Pharmaceuticals is using the assistant to support this process alongside automated performance tracking, creating a feedback cycle that can improve planning over time. 

 As these capabilities mature, the role of supply chain practitioners will evolve as well. Rather than spending most of their time assembling information and manually resolving exceptions, planners can focus on defining objectives, evaluating tradeoffs, challenging assumptions, and making the strategic decisions where human expertise matters most. 

 The best AI strategy starts with the business problem 

 Perhaps the greatest risk in this period of rapid AI development is starting with technology and then searching for a problem to solve. 

 The better approach is to start with the customer problem: understand the outcome that matters, determine how to measure it, and then ask how AI can achieve that outcome in a way that was not possible before. Better decisions can improve product availability, protect customer commitments, strengthen resilience, and unlock growth. 

 As technology expands what businesses can accomplish, innovation must remain grounded in the outcomes customers need. They should hold us accountable not for how many AI agents we develop or how much automation we introduce, but for whether our technology helps them make better decisions, respond faster to change and deliver measurable business outcomes. 

 Devesh Mishra is general manager and chief product officer for SAP Supply Chain Management.

title: From Relational to Semantic: Ontology Modeling on SAP HANA Cloud with metaphactory
author: yashikasomani
text:
Introduction 
 In May 2026, we announced a new strategic technology partnership with metaphacts: the integration of the SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine with metaphactory, an enterprise knowledge graph platform built on open W3C standards. Since that announcement, a key question from customers has been: how do I actually take my existing SAP HANA Cloud data and turn it into a semantic knowledge graph? 
 Drawing on a detailed walkthrough published by our partners at metaphactory, we'll show you how to model an ontology step by step on the metaphactory platform from an existing SAP HANA Cloud schema, with AI assistance throughout. 
 The SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine: Your Semantic Foundation 
 Before we walk through the modeling steps, it is worth briefly grounding the workflow in what the SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine provides. 
 The Knowledge Graph Engine is a dedicated RDF triple store built into SAP HANA Cloud. It stores graph data as subject-predicate-object triples, the foundational data model of the Semantic Web, and it queries that data using SPARQL — the W3C-standardized query language for RDF graphs. Key capabilities include: 
 Native RDF triple store : store and manage knowledge graph data directly inside SAP HANA Cloud, without an external graph database 
 Full SPARQL 1.1 support : query and update RDF data using the same SQL-like fluency your teams already use for relational data 
 SQL–SPARQL interoperability : federate queries across the knowledge graph, relational, vector, and spatial engines in a single platform — no ETL required 
 W3C standards compliance : ontologies expressed in OWL and constraints defined in SHACL are natively supported 
 Fully transactional : the Knowledge Graph Engine participates in SAP HANA Cloud's unified transaction model, reading only committed data 
 Multiple output formats : SPARQL query results can be returned as JSON, XML, CSV, or TSV, making it straightforward to integrate with downstream systems and AI applications 
 For SAP HANA Cloud users, this means your knowledge graph data lives right next to your transactional and analytical data. You don't manage a second system; you extend the one you already have. 
 For full technical details, see the SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine Guide . 
 Getting Started: Supplier Relationship Management 
 The walkthrough below is based on a real example from the metaphactory team: modeling a Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) Ontology on top of an SAP HANA Cloud database. The goal is to create a centralized resource that users from across the enterprise can query and retrieve specific supply chain information and data sources they need. This ontology will help people with and without technical expertise, and also AI, to locate data needed to answer supply chain questions. But like many large enterprises, the information they need is spread across disparate documents and files, all organized and formatted differently. Luckily, because data schemas on the SAP HANA Cloud account capture this valuable information; all of this data can be utilized to build an ontology. 
 Step 1: Connect metaphactory to SAP HANA Cloud & Import Datasource Schema 
 The first step is to create a datasource in metaphactory that points to your SAP HANA Cloud instance. 
 In the metaphactory UI, navigate to the Datasources page and create a new datasource. Give it a descriptive name — in our example, "SRM: Supplier Relationship Management" — and an optional description. Then provide the JDBC connection details for your SAP HANA Cloud instance: 
 JDBC URL : jdbc:sap://<your-hana-host>:<port> 
 Username and Password for your SAP HANA Cloud database user 
 Once the connection details are entered, use the Test Connection button to verify that metaphactory can reach your SAP HANA Cloud instance. Once you have made sure they are connected, you are ready to click “Select Schemas”. 

 Image: SAP HANA Cloud datasource creation and connectivity configuration in metaphactory. 
 With the connection established, the next step is to bring the schema into metaphactory. Click Select Schemas and choose the schema(s) you want to model — in our example, the KGE_USER schema. 
 Press “Create”, and wait for the diagram to load. You will see the main data schema represented as the node “SRM: Supplier Relationship Management: KGE_USER” with six other connected nodes, including the tables inside the data schema such as “PARTNER_CONTACTS”, “PARTNER_ADDRESSES” and “BUSINESS_PARTNERS”. 

 Image: Selecting the schema for the SRM Supplier Relationship Management datasource. 
 Once the import is complete, you will see the schema successfully represented as RDF. 

 Image: Diagram of the loaded datasource schema in metaphactory on SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine. 
 Step 1 Demo: 
 Step 2: Build the Ontology 
 With the schema imported, navigate to the Ontologies section of metaphactory and create a new ontology. Set the title to "Supplier Relationship Management Ontology" and expand the additional metadata and settings and select the data source just created, “SRM: Supplier Relationship Management”. This binding is important: metaphactory's AI assistant metis will use this grounding to suggest an ontology structure that is directly aligned with your actual data. 

 Image: Creating the Supplier Relationship Management Ontology. 
 This is where the workflow starts to feel different from traditional ontology development. 
 metis is metaphactory's AI semantic modeling assistant, built directly into the metaphactory platform. metis combines knowledge from large language models and knowledge graphs to assist you with ontology building via its conversational interface. Following the LOT methodology, it will start by providing the initial context we have for the initial ontology state, and via back-and-forth conversation, metis will help to suggest the ontology structure best suited to your business case needs based on the imported schema — including classes , relations (object properties), and attributes (data properties). 
 For the SRM schema, metis reviews the five tables and generates a set of ontology elements. For example, it might propose: 
 A Supplier class with attributes for name, identifier, and country of origin 
 A Contract class with attributes for start date, end date, and value 
 A Product class linked to suppliers via a suppliedBy relation 
 A PurchaseOrder class linked to contracts via a coveredBy relation 
 metis can also propose competency questions, based on ontology metadata, and the datasource which is used in the context of this ontology. An example question generated in our example is “Which suppliers are currently approved for a given product, service, or category?”. If the ontology fails to answer the proposed questions, you can use the conversational interface to make relevant tweaks, or make manual mapping changes yourself. 
 You review the proposed elements in the metis panel, accept or adjust them, and instruct metis to encode the accepted elements into the ontology. The process is iterative and collaborative: you stay in control of the semantic design while metis does the heavy lifting of translating relational structures into ontology concepts. 

 Image: Using the metis conversational interface to build and refine an ontology. 
 Once you are satisfied with the proposed structure, metis encodes the accepted elements. You now have a formal ontology in OWL, ready for the next step. 
 Step 3: Manual Ontology Building and Refinement 
 Beyond AI-assisted ontology generation, users can also build and enhance ontologies directly using the Visual Ontology Editor. Following a human-in-the-loop approach is strongly recommended to ensure accuracy and quality throughout the modeling process. 
 The metaphactory interface is designed to simplify semantic modeling, allowing users with limited technical expertise to create and manage knowledge graphs efficiently. In this example, we can further enrich the ontology by reviewing the suggestions generated by Metis. These recommendations are available both in the Metis panel and directly on the diagram canvas, where they can be accepted, modified, or removed as needed. 
 For instance, we may decide to add the synonym " Business Partner " to the Supplier class . We can also enhance the class by adding a label attribute with a cardinality of 1. 
 Any modifications made in metaphactory are instantly synchronized with the connected SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine , ensuring that the underlying semantic model always remains up to date. 

 Image: Making manual ontology edits in metaphactory on SAP HANA Knowledge Graph Engine. 
 Step 3 Demo: 
 Step 4: Data Source Mappings in metaphactory 
 An ontology alone describes the shape of your knowledge. To populate it with data from SAP HANA Cloud, you need mappings -- rules that connect relational tables and columns to ontology classes and properties. 
 Navigate to the datasource page, open the Datasource Schema , and create a new mapping set named "SRM mappings" . Select Map Data Schema from the interface, choose the Supplier Relationship Management Ontology from the dropdown, and then enable "Map and Generate AI Mappings" . 
 metaphactory's AI mapping engine analyzes the ontology you built and the relational schema you imported, and automatically generates the mappings between them. Once the generation is complete, you can expand the rows in the data table to explore the generated mappings. 

 Image: Mappings for SRM mappings in metaphactory on SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine. 
 Step 4 Demo: 

 Step 5: Setting up Conversational AI Using metis 
 In this step, we provide a brief overview of how to configure Conversational AI in metaphactory using the SAP HANA Knowledge Graph Engine. 
 To create a Search and Discovery Agent, select AI Services from the toolbar and create a template that includes the Conversational AI component. Once the template has been created, configure the agent by navigating to the Agents and Template & Applications Pages sections in the toolbar and associating the template with the desired agent configuration. 

 Image: Configuring conversational AI on the metaphactory on SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine. 
 Once you have configured your conversational AI, you can begin asking questions about the ontology and connected data sources. For example, if you ask "Describe the class Supplier", metis will process the request and return a summary of the class, including its relevant properties, relationships, and associated metadata. 

 Image: Querying the data schema with the successfully configured conversational AI. 
 Step 5 Demo: 

 Step 6: Exploring Loaded Schema, Ontology and Mappings 
 Now that you have mapped your classes and relationships and refined any corner cases, you are ready to share your ontology with colleagues. They can explore and leverage the ontology through the Conversational AI agent configured in the previous step. The agent utilizes the ontology, the underlying data source, and the mappings you have created to enable users to query source data directly using natural language. 
 Let's explore some additional capabilities of the conversational AI agent. For example, a member of the compliance and regulatory team may need to identify suppliers that present regulatory or business risks. They could ask the search wizard: " Where do I find risk level and financial rating information for suppliers? " 
 The agent would analyze the request and guide the user to the relevant SAP HANA Cloud data schema, specifically the SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) schema imported as KGE_USER, as well as the entities and attributes that are relevant to the question. metis also highlights potential ambiguities and provides additional context that may help users better understand the results. In this example, the attributes RISK_LEVEL and FINANCIAL_RATING are mapped to an Assessment entity rath

title: Intrastat Germany in SAP ECC: transition from IDEV to eSTATISTIK.core – SAP note for SD-FT/MM-FT
author: t_jungesblut75
text:
Hello community, 
 A customer is running SAP ECC 6.0 (classic Foreign Trade, components SD-FT-GOV / MM-FT-GOV) and creates the German Intrastat declarations as INSTAT/XML files: dispatches via VE01 and arrivals via ENPA. So far these files have been uploaded to Destatis via IDEV (form “Außenhandel - D - Intrahandel Dateimeldung”) without any issues. 
 Destatis is moving file submissions in INSTAT/XML format from IDEV to eSTATISTIK.core. When the existing files are checked in .CORE (“Lieferung prüfen”), they are rejected with schema and content errors, for example: 
 declarationTypeCode missing (expected between Function and flowCode) 
 errors in NatureOfTransaction 
 errors in partnerId (dispatches only) 
 in a comparable S/4HANA case also: phoneNumber/faxNumber/e-mail placed directly under ContactPerson instead of ContactPerson/Address, and postalCode/cityName required in that address 
 Question 1: Is there an official SAP solution for ECC? 
 The only note I could find is KBA 3780606 (“Intrastat Germany transition to eSTATISTIK.CORE: xml compliance and required notes”). It refers to SAP S/4HANA (component SLL-ITR-ISR, Intrastat in International Trade / /ECRS/) and fixed the issues in an S/4HANA system. However, it does not seem to apply to the classic Intrastat reports in ECC (VE01/VE03, ENPA). Is there an SAP note or KBA for ECC (SD-FT-GOV / MM-FT-GOV) that makes the INSTAT/XML file compliant with eSTATISTIK.core? Or is SAP not planning a solution for ECC, so that a custom adjustment is required? 
 Question 2: What is the official deadline? 
 I found contradictory information: In a Destatis webinar in August 2025, a transition period of about one year after the start of INSTAT/XML upload in .CORE (September 2025) was mentioned. Some companies were told that IDEV can only be used until the end of 2026. The current information page in the Destatis “Erhebungsportal” states that INSTAT/XML files can be submitted via IDEV up to reference period 2027, and that from reference period January 2028 onwards only .CORE is possible. Does anyone have reliable information, e.g. official communication from Destatis, on which deadline actually applies to existing IDEV file reporters? 
 Thanks in advance for any hints or experiences!
